solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Great admirer I finish with in due course (8)

blocks.note: to do a job is to finish it, as in 'that's that done'

annotation.surface: Someone promises to get round to finishing a fan letter eventually.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finish' is the verb DO, as in 'do the dishes', and 'with' only joins it to the next piece.
annotation.definitionFit: An idolater worships someone or something, so is an admirer of the greatest sort.

entries.clue: Musician to alight, safely evacuated (7)

indicatorNotes.evacuated: an evacuated word has had its contents emptied out, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: to debus is to get off a bus
SAFELY with its insides removed leaves S…Y

annotation.surface: Passengers are told to get off a vehicle and clear it without anyone being hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a bus evacuation drill; 'to alight' is a single verb, DEBUS, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was a French composer.

entries.clue: Man dancing in leotard encapsulates daring (4-7)

indicatorNotes.dancing: letters that dance move about into a new order
indicatorNotes.encapsulates: to encapsulate is to enclose, so the jumbled letters wrap round HE

annotation.surface: A male dancer in a leotard shows a lot of nerve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man dancing' looks like one phrase to jumble; in fact 'Man' is just HE and 'dancing' works on the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Daring is courage, and the lion is the proverbial emblem of a brave heart, as in Richard the Lionheart.

entries.clue: Thrash grasping daughter raised in royal house (5)

indicatorNotes.grasping: to grasp is to hold, so ROUT holds D
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, reading it bottom to top

blocks.note: to rout is to thrash, beat heavily
d = daughter, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A child is beaten and brought up in a palace.
annotation.walkthrough: ROUT holds D to make RODUT, and 'raised' reads that upwards as TUDOR.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

entries.clue: Hemp needed to make these jackets (7)

blocks.note: hemp is cannabis, rolled into joints; the answer names the joints
a reefer is a short, heavy double-breasted jacket

annotation.surface: A tailoring note: hemp cloth is what these jackets are made from.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as hemp the fabric; the first sense wants hemp the drug, rolled into joints.
annotation.definitionFit: A reefer jacket is a sailor's thick double-breasted coat.

entries.clue: Spy conceals missile in oil-producing plant (6)

indicatorNotes.conceals: to conceal is to hide inside, so SEE wraps round SAM

annotation.surface: An agent smuggles a rocket inside a crop at a refinery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spy' looks like an agent, a noun; it is the verb, to see.
annotation.definitionFit: The seeds of this tropical plant are pressed for a cooking oil, which is why the clue calls it oil-producing.

entries.clue: Authorised edition dashed off in panic (9)

blocks.note: a stamped document has been authorised

annotation.surface: An official edition of a book was rushed out in a flap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dashed off' suggests writing something quickly, to match the edition; here it is running away.
annotation.definitionFit: A herd that stampedes rushes off in a panic.

entries.clue: Long blade this killer hides (3)

indicatorNotes.hides: the phrase hides the answer inside its letters

annotation.surface: A murderer is concealing a long knife.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a weapon; the long blade is one you strap to your foot.
annotation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner, a blade for gliding over snow.

entries.clue: Romeo possibly rejecting United’s image (7)

indicatorNotes.rejecting: rejecting a letter throws it out of the word

blocks.note: Romeo Montague, of Romeo and Juliet
U = United, as in football team names; removed

annotation.surface: Perhaps a romantic lead turns down Manchester United's public image.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' looks like the NATO letter R, a trap for the practised solver; here it is Shakespeare's lover, surname Montague.
annotation.definitionFit: A montage is a composite picture made by combining several images.

entries.clue: What father is to son stumbling into a bordello? (5,8)

indicatorNotes.stumbling: stumbling suggests the letters falling about in disorder

annotation.surface: An awkward scene: a father and son run into each other entering a brothel.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as the definition, but the letters of 'into a bordello' supply the answer; 'son stumbling' hides that 'stumbling' acts on what follows.
annotation.definitionFit: Father and son share ancestry by descent, which is kinship by birth rather than by marriage.

entries.clue: Job to follow this husband entering compound (6)

indicatorNotes.entering: H enters the compound, going inside it

blocks.note: an ester is a chemical compound

annotation.surface: A husband joins a chemical plant, with a job lined up for later.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like work; it is the Book of Job, which follows the Book of Esther in the Old Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: In the Bible the Book of Job comes straight after the Book of Esther.

entries.clue: Particular paranormal power periodically perceivable (8)

indicatorNotes.periodically: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

annotation.surface: A certain psychic gift can be sensed only now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: The alliterative run of P words dresses up a plain charade.
annotation.definitionFit: Especial is an old-fashioned word for particular or special.

entries.clue: 2’s work, used originally in adaptation of Cinderella (5,2,4)

indicatorNotes.originally: the original letter of a word is its first
indicatorNotes.in: U goes in among the letters being rearranged
indicatorNotes.adaptation of: an adaptation reworks the material into a new form

annotation.surface: A composer's piece was used in a stage version of the fairy tale.
annotation.walkthrough: '2' points to the answer at 2 down, DEBUSSY; his best-known piano piece is Clair de Lune.
annotation.definitionFit: Clair de Lune is the third movement of Debussy's Suite bergamasque.

entries.clue: Oppressed girl lives in city near Sidon with duke (10)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' as a preposition of place puts ANN IS inside the city TYRE

blocks.note: Tyre and Sidon are neighbouring Phoenician cities in Lebanon

annotation.surface: A girl downtrodden in an ancient Levantine city, alongside a nobleman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lives in' reads as one phrase about where the girl lives; it splits into IS and the container instruction 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tyrant rules harshly, and a people so ruled are oppressed.

entries.clue: Church wine consumed by wild Scots? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: RED is eaten, taken inside NO TAME

blocks.note: wild = not tame, which a Scot would say as 'no tame'

annotation.surface: Some communion wine is drunk by unruly Scotsmen.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the Scots idiom: in Scotland 'no' often stands for 'not', as in 'I'm no sure'.
annotation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the great cathedral church in Paris.

entries.clue: Poet dispensing with uniform in Arabian port (4)

indicatorNotes.dispensing with: to dispense with something is to do without it, so U is dropped

blocks.note: U = uniform in the NATO alphabet; removed

annotation.surface: A poet goes about out of uniform in a Yemeni harbour town.
annotation.walkthrough: AUDEN is the crossword's favourite poet; losing U leaves the port.
annotation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula.

entries.clue: Small disagreement — is it over a shoe? (4)

blocks.note: a cloth gaiter buttoned over the top of a shoe, Edwardian menswear

annotation.surface: A couple bicker, and the row is about footwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like 'about'; the second sense is a spat literally covering the shoe.
annotation.definitionFit: A spat is a minor quarrel; spats were short gaiters buttoned over the shoe.

entries.clue: Quick securing border for dominance (7)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure is to hold firmly, so PACY holds RIM

blocks.note: a rim is a border or edge

annotation.surface: A fast frontier grab to seize control.
annotation.walkthrough: PACY is British sports talk for quick, as of a winger or bowler.
annotation.definitionFit: Primacy is the state of being first, pre-eminence or dominance.

entries.clue: Below zero inside so like stormy weather (10)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' places one thing within another, so UNDER O sits within THUS

annotation.surface: Temperatures below freezing make it feel like a storm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Below zero' reads as sub-zero weather; it is UNDER and O.
annotation.definitionFit: Thunderous means resembling thunder, the noise of a storm.

entries.clue: Really poor mandate for saving the planet? (7)

blocks.note: hopeless, very bad, as in 'he's really poor at maths'
read as two words, the green command to consume less

annotation.surface: A feeble environmental policy is dismissed as worthless.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second sense as a pun: USELESS split as USE LESS is the conservationist's order.
annotation.definitionFit: Useless means of no use, very poor.

entries.clue: With ego Trump nearly upset an idealist (7)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly all of the word: drop its last letter
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, reading them upwards

blocks.note: Trump was POTUS, President of the United States; nearly gives POTU, upset UTOP

annotation.surface: An egotistical president almost upsets a dreamer.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads Trump as the man himself; the wordplay wants his title, POTUS.
annotation.definitionFit: A utopian is a visionary who believes in an ideal society.

entries.clue: Imagination detective attached to objects (5,3)

blocks.note: to object is to mind: 'she minds' = 'she objects'
a private eye is a detective

annotation.surface: A detective with a gift for picturing things is linked to some evidence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a plural noun, things; it is the verb, minds. 'Attached to' puts EYE after it.
annotation.definitionFit: The mind's eye is the faculty of picturing things, imagination.

indicatorNotes.attached to: one piece is fixed on to the end of the other, so EYE follows MINDS

entries.clue: Divine being in form — demand regularly to be recalled (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at a regular interval, every other one
indicatorNotes.to be recalled: recalling calls something back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: iN fOrM dEmAnD, the even letters

annotation.surface: A god-like figure on top form insists on being remembered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In form' looks like part of the definition; its letters start the regular pick.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a daemon is a lesser divinity or guiding spirit.

entries.clue: Dorothy Parker leaving land for admirer (5)

indicatorNotes.leaving: PARK leaves PARKER, dropping out of it

blocks.note: PARKER without PARK, parkland being land

annotation.surface: The American wit Dorothy Parker sails away to find a fan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dorothy Parker' is the writer, one name; the wordplay splits it into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A doter is someone who dotes, a fond admirer.

entries.clue: Star system’s unstable nuclear path captured by artificial intelligence (5,8)

indicatorNotes.unstable: unstable letters won't stay put and fall into a new order
indicatorNotes.captured by: the jumbled letters are held inside AI

annotation.surface: A robot seizes control of a runaway reactor's route through the stars.
annotation.walkthrough: The science-fiction surface fits the answer, which is the nearest star system to the Sun.
annotation.definitionFit: Alpha Centauri is a triple star system, our nearest stellar neighbour.

entries.clue: Set down, winning over time (3)

blocks.note: a team that is up is winning

annotation.surface: A match report: recorded as a victory, in extra time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winning over' reads as persuading; it splits into UP and the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to set a thing down somewhere is to place or put it there.

entries.clue: Plant all borders in magically radiant landscape (6)

indicatorNotes.all borders: the borders of every word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: MagicallY, its first and last letters
RadianT, its first and last letters
LandscapE, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A gardener plants every flowerbed in a dazzling scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borders' is gardening talk here, so 'Plant' reads as a verb; it is the noun, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen flowering shrub.

entries.clue: NCO awfully strange when ingesting Ecstasy (8)

indicatorNotes.awfully: done awfully, badly, the letters come out jumbled
indicatorNotes.ingesting: to ingest is to take in, so the jumble holds E

annotation.surface: A corporal behaves very oddly after taking a pill.
annotation.walkthrough: NCO is a non-commissioned officer, such as a corporal or sergeant.
annotation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer.
